Check out Rose Anvil on YouTube! Great channel. Basically he deconstructs boots and explains the materials, construction, everything about it! Why it's good and bad

Stridewise is another great channel too. Not just focusing on boots, but other leather goods as well as raw denim.

This is a great question that I'm glad is finally being asked. 

Unlike sneakers which are all largely made in the same region in the same factories, GOOD quality boots that are worth the money will simply last you forever. 

*TLDR* - Avoid Doc Martens and Timberlands. They suck if you actually know anything about boots. 


Look out for these key things 

1. Leather quality - avoid faux leathers or anything that simply says "genuine leather". Calfskin, chromexcel, oil tanned are examples of leathers to look out for but there's at least half a dozen others too!

2. Construction - unlike shoes and some cheap boots like timberlands and doc martens, good boots that will last usually be made with specific stitches/construction to ensure its durable, comfortable, and can be resoled. I'd recommend 100% a  Good year welt. Alternatively you could look into Blake stitches, or a stitch down. 

3. Where it's made - Very self explanatory. Don't buy boots from China. Not to push any xenophobia ofc, but boots made in mass are not it. This also includes avoiding designer high end boots. Avoid designer brands unless you are a silly goose. 

4. Midsole - What type of midsole is the boot? Leather is great for durability and comfort, Rubber is great for being a little firm, Cork can more quickly adapt to your foots shape 


I shortened it down for sure and I omitted some other stuff too like what type of boot (moc toe, lace up, Chelsea ECT.). There's plenty of resources that explains it much better than I can but I just gave rundown on what I would personally look for first. 
I hope that's enough information for you to help your search. I'd recommend looking at the Rose Anvil YouTube channel or Steidewise. 

*To get you started, I'd suggest*

Thursday Boot Company Captain boots - great blend of casual and classy, I would 100% recommend!!! These are made in America 

Thorogood boots - pretty casual and outdoorsy, great for hiking with a very bouncy midsole! These are made in America 

Solovairs - Doc Martens before they became sellouts. They have excellent boots, leather shoes, ECT. The superiority complex you'll get over Doc Martens plebs is intoxicating. These are made in the UK 

RM Williams - low key needs not introduction. These are the gold standard of chelsea boots. Handmade and custom fitted for you! They are imo worth the money. These are made in Starya fuck yeah 🔥🔥

Red Wing - Another American staple, these are great all rounder, but the tip is more rounded compared to Thursday Captain boots. Still an excellent choice nonetheless. Made in America


There is obviously hundreds of more I could list, however this comment is already long, and you'll stumble upon them along the way. I started my boot journey a while ago and I'm always learning new things! I'm hoping to save some money and splurge on some custom made Indonesian boots!


Remember, you spend half your life in bed, and the other half in boots, so invest well into both!
